intent: A thin rule dividing groups of rows inside a context menu popup.
typical_uses: The divider between two groups of related actions, or before a destructive action

dont_use_when.situation: A divider in page layout or inside a card, outside any menu

invariants.text: context-menu.module.css pulls the rule out by the popup's padding on both sides, so it runs edge to edge across the popup, and gives it vertical margin of its own.
context-menu.module.css draws only a horizontal rule; `orientation` changes the announced orientation, not the drawing.
The separator renders with role `separator`, takes no pointer events and is not a row that arrow keys land on.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the separator's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the separator's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (orientation). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through context-menu.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A separator before a destructive action

bad.title: The page-level Separator used inside the menu
bad.why: ContextMenuContent does not accept Separator; the page-level separator carries none of this menu's spacing and stops at the popup's padding instead of running edge to edge.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, SeparatorState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through context-menu.module.css, not through this.
